title: The scales of physics
caption: Lengths in physics run from the Planck length (~10⁻³⁵ m) to the observable universe (~10²⁷ m), about 62 orders of magnitude. Each step on the scale is a factor of 10⁵. Quantum mechanics is needed at atomic scales and below; classical mechanics works for everyday sizes; general relativity takes over for strong gravity and the universe as a whole.
alt: A logarithmic length scale from 10^-36 to 10^28 metres with the Planck length, a proton, an atom, a virus, a person, the Earth, the Earth–Sun distance, the Milky Way and the observable universe marked, over bands for quantum, classical and cosmological physics.
description: A horizontal logarithmic scale of length in metres: each tick is 100 000 times the one before.

Marked from smallest to largest: Planck length 1.6 × 10⁻³⁵ m, proton 1.7 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, hydrogen atom 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m, virus 10⁻⁷ m, person 1.7 m, Earth 1.3 × 10⁷ m, Earth–Sun distance 1.5 × 10¹¹ m, Milky Way 10²¹ m, observable universe 8.8 × 10²⁶ m: about 62 orders of magnitude.

Bands under the scale show the regime of each theory: quantum mechanics below about 10⁻⁸ m, classical mechanics for everyday sizes, general relativity and cosmology for astronomical sizes. The boundaries are rough: what decides is the situation, not only the size.
